sections.h2: What kind of place is Whiteside County for a house seller?
sections.html:
Whiteside County stretches across 697 square miles of northwestern Illinois, and the Mississippi River marks its western edge. Morrison holds the courthouse, while Sterling is the biggest city. Rock Falls, Fulton and Prophetstown are the other cities, and the villages include Albany, Erie, Lyndon and Tampico, where Ronald Reagan was born in 1911.

The county dates to 1836, when pieces of Jo Daviess and Henry counties were joined, and the borders have stayed put. The Morrison climate record shows January days averaging a low near 10 degrees, and July highs around 85.

Together the county makes up the Sterling micropolitan area. Carroll, Ogle, Lee, Bureau, Henry and Rock Island counties border it in Illinois, with Clinton County, Iowa, across the river, so buyers may arrive from several tax systems and compare bills.

Your total depends on the parcel's township, one of 22, and on every district layered over it. A city lot and a township-road farmhouse can carry quite different totals at the same assessed value.

sections.h2: What do Whiteside County housing figures look like?
sections.html:
Whiteside County values run lower than most of Illinois. The midpoint owner-occupied home was valued at $127,100 across 2020 to 2024, and 76.9% of homes are occupied by their owners.

sections.h2: Who bills and who assesses in Whiteside County?
sections.html:
The County Collector sends a single bill for each parcel and then splits the money among more than 140 taxing districts. For the 2024 taxes payable in 2025, the total to be collected was $101,388,931.80, and $98,835,123.12 of it was real estate tax.

  • Collector and Treasurer: 200 East Knox Street in Morrison, phone 815-772-5196, weekday hours listed as 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: sets assessments, handles exemptions and takes address changes. The county website lists the office and its phone.
  • The Collector has no say over your valuation, the bill's size, exemptions or your mailing address.

A bill arrives even when your lender pays from escrow, and the county keeps no mortgage records, so direct escrow questions to the lender. For a new mailing address, send the county's change-of-address form to the Supervisor of Assessments.

sections.h2: How does the Whiteside County tax calendar run?
sections.html:
The year splits into a June installment and a September installment. For 2026 the county mailed bills May 15, set June 17 and September 1 as the due dates, and started penalties the next day each time. The mobile home due date was June 1. The calendar also listed the annual tax sale for November 5, 2026.

The county's tax cycle page lays out why the sequence works that way. Local taxing districts begin their fiscal years on different dates: municipalities on May 1, school districts on July 1 and counties on December 1. Each body adopts a levy ordinance, the County Clerk calculates rates and extends the bill for every taxpayer, and the Treasurer prepares the roll. Past-due accounts pass to the State's Attorney and County Treasurer, and tax buyers file for judgment and run the sale.

Part-payments are refused. Send a whole installment as printed, or the full year by the first date, with the tax stub attached so the check is not returned.

sections.h2: What payment methods does the Whiteside County Collector accept?
sections.html:
The county's payment sheet names several channels, and each carries its own cutoff.

  • Over the counter at the Treasurer's office in the courthouse during its regular hours.
  • Through the mail, where a postmark dated by the deadline avoids penalty. The county takes no responsibility for lost mail.
  • Automatic ACH debit on every due date, canceled only by a written request.
  • Credit card with a 2.25% surcharge, or e-check with a flat $1.50.
  • At banks on the participating list, bill in hand, up to a cutoff that the 2026 sheet put at September 1.
  • In the drop box just inside the Morrison courthouse's Law Enforcement Center entrance, before 4:30 on the due date.

Write checks to the Whiteside County Collector. A returned check adds $25.00 on top of penalties, and personal checks are not taken in the month before the tax sale.

sections.h2: How are Whiteside County homes assessed, and how can you appeal?
sections.html:
The assessor's FAQ says Illinois values property at one-third of market value, or 33.3%. A bill is the final equalized assessed value, less exemptions, multiplied by the rate. An equalization factor evens out the 22 townships, and valuations rest on the prior three years of sales as of January 1, which explains why a bill can rise even when prices dip.

To challenge a figure, set it beside an appraisal or beside recent sales of comparable houses, then raise it with the Supervisor of Assessments office. A formal appeal goes to the Board of Review in writing, inside thirty days after the township publishes, which tracks section 16-55 of the Property Tax Code.

Additions raise value. The office gets copies of building permits and inspects the work in the field. A home improvement exemption softens the increase for four years, up to $25,000 of assessed value, and appears as an adjustment on the bill.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Whiteside County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Whiteside is far from Cook County, so the standard dollar caps apply.

  • General homestead: a reduction of up to $6,000 in equalized assessed value on an owner's residence (section 15-175).
  • Senior citizens: up to $5,000 more, once an owner reaches 65 (section 15-170).
  • Low-income senior freeze: ties a qualifying older owner's assessment to a base year (section 15-172).

Missing exemption? Ask the Supervisor of Assessments to review the parcel. After a sale the break lasts to the end of that assessment year, and the buyer may need to apply for the next.

sections.h2: What happens with Whiteside County back taxes when a house sells?
sections.html:
Late installments bear interest of 1 1/2% per month or part of one (section 21-15). A postmark by the due date keeps a mailed payment on time.

Open taxes can be sold at the annual sale. The owner may then redeem for up to three years, with exceptions in section 21-350.

  • Ask the Collector for the exact balance, penalty included, ahead of signing a contract.
  • Let the closing agent wire the payoff from your proceeds.
  • A parcel already sold at a tax sale needs a redemption quote and a deadline from the county.

Search by parcel number, not by name. A stale mailing address or an inherited house is where a balance tends to hide.

faqs.q: What are the Whiteside County tax due dates?
faqs.a: June and September, each with its own date. In 2026 those were June 17 and September 1. The Collector's page carries the calendar for whichever cycle is current.

faqs.q: Can I use a credit card in Whiteside County?
faqs.a: Yes, with a surcharge. Paying by check, in person or by ACH debit skips the surcharge entirely.

faqs.q: Does Whiteside County accept a partial payment?
faqs.a: No. An installment is accepted only in the printed amount, and both may be combined in one payment by the first due date.

faqs.q: How do I challenge a Whiteside County valuation?
faqs.a: Put the complaint in writing and deliver it to the Board of Review inside thirty days after your township publishes. Gather an appraisal or comparable sales beforehand, and bring questions to the assessor's office.

faqs.q: What if I sell a Whiteside County house owing tax?
faqs.a: Call the Collector at 815-772-5196 for a payoff and settle it from the proceeds. Interest keeps adding monthly until the balance clears, so closing is the natural time to pay.
